summary: Mara forced the attic hatch open with a crowbar after it stuck on the second pull; hands already raw from hauling boxes (quote: "The hatch stuck on the second pull. My hands were already raw ... so I used the crowbar the estate agent had left in the garage and pried the thing up in two impatient breaths.").

Mara opened the largest trunk and found a small tarnished brass locket on a fragile chain on a pad of yellowing tissue, and a larger sepia photograph folded in a moth-eaten handkerchief (quote: "Inside, on a pad of yellowing tissue, lay a small, tarnished brass locket on a fragile chain and, beside it, a larger sepia photograph folded carefully in a moth-eaten handkerchief.").

Mara noticed a second figure in the mirror's reflection — a girl at the far end of the attic — which did not mirror Mara's movements (quote: "There, at the far end of the attic ... the glass held a second figure ... The girl did not move in unison; she stayed at the far end, a pale, steady shape in the glass.").
